- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.3) — reduce forecast slightly to avoid overreaction.
- Underestimate prices after strong downward spikes (sentiment < 0.1) — add a small upward bias to account for mean reversion.
- Overshoot after recent price spikes — cap forecast at 1–2% below peak if sentiment is neutral or slightly bearish.
- Lagged price movements often overcorrect — adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of true values.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), reduce forecast volatility — smooth out sharp peaks and troughs.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast, especially after 10+ days of rising prices, apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (avg < 0.1) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day to avoid false optimism.
